products.name: Pinecone
products.note: Vector database; RAG infrastructure; data residency options; enterprise security

reading.body:
Pinecone provides vector database infrastructure that enables AI systems to search billions of items for semantic matches in milliseconds, a capability foundational to retrieval-augmented generation at scale.

Vector databases sit between raw compute and useful AI output. A language model generates tokens, but retrieval-augmented generation requires the ability to fetch relevant context from massive datasets faster than traditional search allows. Pinecone's product addresses this by indexing data so that semantic similarity queries remain fast as dataset size grows. This is not a compute constraint problem, but it is a compute efficiency problem. Without fast retrieval infrastructure, the same query would force a model to process far more tokens to achieve the same accuracy, wasting the compute that has already been purchased.

The data provided does not cover Pinecone's infrastructure footprint, the power consumption of its service, or the buildings that host it. It does not reveal whether Pinecone runs on its own hardware or rents compute from cloud providers, and therefore does not establish how directly grid constraints affect its ability to scale. The company's 311 law exposure cases in New York are noted but not detailed, leaving their nature and impact unclear.

profile_text.body:
Pinecone describes itself as the trusted AI knowledge company. Its AI knowledge platform, made up of Database, Nexus, and Marketplace, is said to power accurate, fast, cost-effective AI for 10,000+ customers and 1M developers worldwide. The company also describes Pinecone as a fully managed vector database built for AI, with instantly searchable writes, automatic indexing, and queries that stay fast at any scale.

Pinecone was founded in 2019 and is headquartered in New York, NY, US. Its product is described as a vector database with RAG infrastructure, data residency options, and enterprise security.

The company has 458 law exposure records in New York. No litigation cases are listed.
